title: `demolish node` with no name indexes fields[2] out of bounds
detail: Input `demolish node` has len(fields)==2, so it passes the `< 2` guard; fields[1]=="node" is true, then fields[2] is out of bounds — a runtime panic, not the clean parse error the file's "typo'd demo must fail loudly" contract promises. One bad line aborts the whole batch.
recommended_fix: Guard the node form separately: require len(fields) >= 3 before reading fields[2], returning a parse error otherwise (mirror the other verb arity checks).

title: Unreachable duplicate `if !os.exists(path)` after an early return
detail: The second `if !os.exists(path)` immediately follows a block that returns on that identical condition, so it can never be true. It is dead code that only obscures the real control flow.
recommended_fix: Delete the redundant `if !os.exists(path) { /* handled above */ }` line.

title: write_file and write_log are byte-identical procedures
detail: write_file and write_log have identical signatures, bodies, and even the same doc comment. Two names for one operation is a maintenance hazard — a future fix to one won't reach the other.
recommended_fix: Delete write_log and replace its single call site in main.odin (`write_log(...log.bin...)`) with write_file.

title: verify_replay stubs the fixture flag: dead `bar`, unused param, hardcoded `bare=false`
detail: `bar` is declared then immediately discarded; `demo_name` is never used in the body; and `bare=false` is hardcoded. The comment claims the fixture is carried by the demo, but nothing reads it — so a bare demo replays under the non-bare (six-node) fixture and its hashes diverge from tick 1.
recommended_fix: Thread the demo's map_fixture (or a bare bool) into verify_replay and pass it to replay_hashes's `bare` arg; remove `bar` and the now-false comment.

title: place_router silently drops non-numeric coordinates (parse_i64 ok ignored)
evidence:
case "place_router":
		if len(fields) < 4 { return it, fmt.tprintf("line %d: place_router type x y", ln) }
		it.a = strings.clone(fields[1])
		it.x, _ = strconv.parse_i64(fields[2])
		it.y, _ = strconv.parse_i64(fields[3])
detail: The ok flag from parse_i64 is discarded for both coordinates; a non-numeric x or y silently becomes 0. This contradicts the file header's strict-by-contract rule that a typo'd demo must fail loudly rather than be silently coerced.
recommended_fix: Capture and check the ok flag for both coords (`x, ok := strconv.parse_i64(fields[2]); if !ok { return it, fmt.tprintf(...) }`) and reject malformed input.

title: check_golden leaks `img` in the mismatch branches (only freed on match)
detail: `img` is unloaded only in the match (else) branch. In both mismatch branches it is handed to save_diff_bundle (whose body never calls UnloadImage on `actual`) and then never freed — an asymmetric leak of a raylib-allocated image per failing capture.
recommended_fix: Unload img unconditionally after the if/else (it is consumed before that point in every branch), or give save_diff_bundle clear non-owning semantics.

title: parse_expect silently accepts a malformed `within <window>` clause
detail: If the window token lacks `..`, `range` length is not 2 and there is no else branch — lo_ms/hi_ms silently stay 0, so the expectation only matches events at tick 0. A malformed `within` clause is accepted instead of rejected, against the strict-parse contract.
recommended_fix: Add an else branch that returns a parse error when `within` is present but the range doesn't split into exactly two valid ms values.
